symbols.name: J
symbols.def: the fixed number of treatment actions

symbols.name: d
symbols.def: the fixed dimension of the assignment parameter

symbols.name: L
symbols.def: the fixed number of cross-fitting folds

symbols.name: \(c_{\min}\)
symbols.def: the smallest direct KL penalty coordinate

symbols.name: \(c_{\max}\)
symbols.def: the largest direct KL penalty coordinate

symbols.name: \(s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}\)
symbols.def: the positive welfare scale used by FangRidderXie2026 to report its normalized preference index

symbols.name: \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}\)
symbols.def: the coefficient multiplying KL divergence in the FangRidderXie2026 optimization criterion

symbols.name: \(\mathcal O\)
symbols.def: the observed-data sample space induced by \(\mathcal X\), \(\mathcal A\), and \([-B,B]\)

symbols.name: \(\nu\)
symbols.space: finitely supported probability laws on \(\mathcal O\)
symbols.def: an auxiliary finitely supported law used to state uniform covering bounds

symbols.name: \(b_a\)
symbols.def: the planner's prespecified positive benchmark weight \(b_a(x)\) for action \(a\) at covariate value \(x\)

symbols.name: \(G\)
symbols.def: the Gaussian process with covariance kernel \(\Gamma\)

symbols.name: \(r_{m,n}\)
symbols.def: an \(L^2(P_X)\) estimability rate for the outcome regressions

symbols.name: \(r_{e,n}\)
symbols.def: an \(L^2(P_X)\) estimability rate for the observational propensities

symbols.name: \(\widehat m_a^{(-\ell)}\)
symbols.def: a learner trained outside \(\mathcal I_\ell\) that attains rate \(r_{m,n}\)

symbols.name: \(\widehat e_a^{(-\ell)}\)
symbols.def: a learner trained outside \(\mathcal I_\ell\) that attains rate \(r_{e,n}\)

symbols.name: \(\widehat v_i\)
symbols.def: for \(i\in\mathcal I_\ell\), \(\widehat v_i(\theta)=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\pi_\theta(a\mid X_i)\widehat m_a^{(-\ell)}(X_i)+\pi_\theta(A_i\mid X_i)\{\widehat e_{A_i}^{(-\ell)}(X_i)\}^{-1}\{Y_i-\widehat m_{A_i}^{(-\ell)}(X_i)\}\)

symbols.name: \(\widehat v_\theta^{(-\ell)}\)
symbols.def: \(\widehat v_\theta^{(-\ell)}(O)=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\pi_\theta(a\mid X)\widehat m_a^{(-\ell)}(X)+\pi_\theta(A\mid X)\{\widehat e_A^{(-\ell)}(X)\}^{-1}\{Y-\widehat m_A^{(-\ell)}(X)\}\)

symbols.name: \(\widehat H_c^{\mathrm{tot}}\)
symbols.def: Let \(\widehat\lambda_{\min}(c)=\lambda_{\min}(\widehat H_c)\) and set \(\widehat H_c^{\mathrm{tot}}=\widehat H_c+\{h/2-\widehat\lambda_{\min}(c)\}_+I_d\). This measurable ridge fallback has smallest eigenvalue at least \(h/2\) for every sample and every \(c\), and equals \(\widehat H_c\) whenever \(\widehat\lambda_{\min}(c)\ge h/2\).

symbols.name: \(\widetilde\Psi_i\)
symbols.def: the foldwise plug-in version of \(\Psi_c(O_i)\) obtained by substituting \(\widehat\theta_c\), \(\widehat m^{(-\ell)}\), \(\widehat e^{(-\ell)}\), empirical gradients, and \((\widehat H_c^{\mathrm{tot}})^{-1}\) for every occurrence of \(H_c^{-1}\), then subtracting its empirical mean at each \(c\)

symbols.name: \(C_{\mathrm{sm}}\)
symbols.def: a constant depending only on the fixed action count, feature and outcome bounds, overlap and benchmark lower bounds, compact parameter neighborhood, and inverse-curvature bound

symbols.name: \(\mathsf N_n\)
symbols.def: \(\mathsf N_n(\varepsilon)\) is the smallest number of open \(\widehat d_n\)-balls of radius \(\varepsilon\) covering \(\mathcal C\)

symbols.name: \(\xi_i\)
symbols.def: independent across \(i\) and independent of the data

symbols.name: \(s\)
symbols.def: a continuous coordinatewise scale bounded above and away from zero

symbols.name: \(\widehat{\mathcal T}_n\)
symbols.def: \(\widehat{\mathcal T}_n=\{(c,w,k):c\in\mathcal C,\ |w-\widehat W(\widehat\theta_c)|\le s_W(c)(\widehat q_{1-\alpha}+\eta)/\sqrt n,\ |k-\widehat K(\widehat\theta_c)|\le s_K(c)(\widehat q_{1-\alpha}+\eta)/\sqrt n\}\)

symbols.name: \(\widehat c\)
symbols.def: an arbitrary measurable function of the plotted sample path

symbols.name: \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_n(k)\)
symbols.def: \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_n(k)=\{c\in\mathcal C:|\widehat K(\widehat\theta_c)-k|\le s_K(c)(\widehat q_{1-\alpha}+\eta)/\sqrt n\}\)

symbols.name: \(\widehat{\mathcal V}_n(k)\)
symbols.def: \(\widehat{\mathcal V}_n(k)=\bigcup_{c\in\widehat{\mathcal C}_n(k)}[\widehat W(\widehat\theta_c)-s_W(c)(\widehat q_{1-\alpha}+\eta)/\sqrt n,\widehat W(\widehat\theta_c)+s_W(c)(\widehat q_{1-\alpha}+\eta)/\sqrt n]\)

symbols.name: \(Q\)
symbols.def: \(Q(c)=\tfrac12G_\theta(c)^\top H_cG_\theta(c)\), where \(G_\theta\) is the optimizer coordinate of \(G\)

assumptions.condition: \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and identically distributed with law \(P\).
\(|Y(a)|\le B\) almost surely for every \(a\in\mathcal A\).

novel.justification: This note maintains path-uniform interiority, which is stronger than fixed-penalty interiority. A concrete sufficient route is that the unique interior optimizer depends continuously on \(c\), \(\mathcal C\) is compact, and its image lies in the interior of \(\Theta\); continuity of the boundary-distance map then gives a positive uniform \(\rho\). This holds, for example, when bounded features and outcomes and a benchmark bounded away from zero yield a continuous softmax criterion and the optimizer image is contained in a compact subset of \(\operatorname{int}(\Theta)\).

assumptions.condition: \((c,\theta)\mapsto M_c(\theta)\) is three times continuously differentiable in \(\theta\) on a fixed neighborhood of \(\{(c,\theta_c):c\in\mathcal C\}\), with uniformly continuous third derivative.

novel.justification: This note maintains three derivatives uniformly along the path, which is stronger than the two-derivative fixed-penalty smoothness used by FangRidderXie2026. In the finite-action softmax subclass, bounded features, bounded outcomes, benchmark weights bounded away from zero, compact \(\mathcal C\), and a compact parameter neighborhood make the log-partition map analytic in \(\theta\); finite sums and dominated differentiation then give continuous derivatives through order three, and compactness makes the third derivative uniformly continuous.

This note maintains a single curvature floor over the compact preference path, which is stronger than FangRidderXie2026's pointwise Hessian condition at one fixed penalty. Bounded features and outcomes, benchmark weights bounded away from zero, and the three-derivative condition make \(c\mapsto H_c\) continuous along a continuous optimizer path; positive definiteness at every \(c\in\mathcal C\) then yields \(h>0\) by compactness. A concrete benchmark-near sufficient design has a uniform positive eigenvalue floor for the centered-feature covariance on the optimizer neighborhood, a neighborhood small enough to control the third-cumulant term in the KL Hessian, and a welfare-Hessian upper bound strictly smaller than \(c_{\min}\) times the resulting KL-curvature floor.

assumptions.condition: For every nonzero \(v\in\mathbb R^d\), \(P_X\{\operatorname{Var}_{\pi_\theta}(v^\top q_A(X)\mid X)>0\}>0\) for every \(\theta\) in the optimizer neighborhood.
Each \(m_a\) is \(L^2(P_X)\)-estimable at the deterministic rate \(r_{m,n}\to0\), uniformly over the fixed set \(\mathcal A\).
Each \(e_a\) is \(L^2(P_X)\)-estimable at the deterministic rate \(r_{e,n}\to0\), uniformly over the fixed set \(\mathcal A\).
\(\min_{1\le\ell\le L}|\mathcal I_\ell|/n\) is bounded away from zero.

definitions.name: benchmark-centered softmax rule
definitions.construction: For every \(\theta\in\Theta\), set \(\pi_\theta(a\mid x)=b_a(x)\exp\{\theta^\top q_a(x)\}/\sum_{r\in\mathcal A}b_r(x)\exp\{\theta^\top q_r(x)\}\).

definitions.name: oracle welfare--divergence path
definitions.construction: For each \(c\in\mathcal C\), maximize \(M_c(\theta)=W(\theta)-cK(\theta)\) over \(\Theta\), and set \(\tau(c)=(\theta_c,W(\theta_c),K(\theta_c))\).

definitions.name: Fang--Ridder--Xie penalty correspondence
definitions.construction: At a deterministic coordinate \(c\in\mathcal C\), identify this proposal's direct KL penalty with the comparator's optimization penalty by \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c\). The corresponding preference reported by FangRidderXie2026 is therefore \(c_{\mathrm{FRX}}=\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}=c/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}\). The common-submodel comparison restricts their admissible-rule framework to the finite-action benchmark-centered softmax subclass \(\{\pi_\theta:\theta\in\Theta\}\).

definitions.name: cross-fitted doubly robust frontier estimator
definitions.construction: Choose foldwise learners attaining \(r_{m,n}\) and \(r_{e,n}\), clip the outcome learner to \([-B,B]\), clip the propensity learner below at \(\epsilon/2\), construct \(\widehat v_i\), \(\widehat W\), and \(\widehat K\) as declared, and set \(\widehat\theta_c\in\arg\max_{\theta\in\Theta}\{\widehat W(\theta)-c\widehat K(\theta)\}\) and \(\widehat\tau(c)=(\widehat\theta_c,\widehat W(\widehat\theta_c),\widehat K(\widehat\theta_c))\).

definitions.name: measurable totalized empirical Hessian
definitions.construction: For each \(c\in\mathcal C\), let \(\widehat\lambda_{\min}(c)=\lambda_{\min}(\widehat H_c)\) and set \(\widehat H_c^{\mathrm{tot}}=\widehat H_c+\{h/2-\widehat\lambda_{\min}(c)\}_+I_d\). Use \((\widehat H_c^{\mathrm{tot}})^{-1}\) in every plug-in optimizer influence, and use the resulting common centered influence stack in \(\widehat\Gamma\), \(G_n^*\), and \(Q_n^*\).

definitions.name: foldwise random-class replacement handle
definitions.construction: Condition on one training complement at a time. For \(u\in\{0,1,2\}\), use the classes \(\mathcal F_{\ell,u}\) to obtain conditional-mean bounds of order \(C_{\mathrm{sm}}r_{m,n}r_{e,n}\), conditional \(L^2(P)\) envelope bounds of order \(C_{\mathrm{sm}}(r_{m,n}+r_{e,n})\), and fixed-dimensional polynomial entropy. Combine these bounds with the explicitly defined path plug-in radius \(\upsilon_n\) to target \(\delta_n\le C_{\mathrm{sm}}\{r_{m,n}+r_{e,n}+r_{m,n}r_{e,n}+\upsilon_n\}+o_{\mathbb P}(1)\); use empirical curvature for \(\Lambda_n=O_{\mathbb P}(1)\), apply a conditional Gaussian maximal inequality to the multiplier difference, and sum the fixed number \(L\) of fold bounds without asserting independence across folds.

definitions.name: shared estimated-influence multiplier bootstrap
definitions.construction: Form every optimizer-influence coordinate with the total ridge convention \((\widehat H_c^{\mathrm{tot}})^{-1}\), center the resulting foldwise plug-in vectors to obtain \(\widetilde\Psi_i(c)\), draw one common multiplier vector \((\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_n)\), and calculate \(G_n^*(c)=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\xi_i\widetilde\Psi_i(c)\) for every \(c\in\mathcal C\). The same totalized influences define \(\widehat\Gamma\) and \(G_n^*\).

definitions.name: simultaneous welfare--divergence tube
definitions.construction: Use the conditional quantile \(\widehat q_{1-\alpha}\) of the shared multiplier supremum and fixed slack \(\eta\) to form \(\widehat{\mathcal T}_n=\{(c,w,k):|w-\widehat W(\widehat\theta_c)|\le s_W(c)(\widehat q_{1-\alpha}+\eta)/\sqrt n,\ |k-\widehat K(\widehat\theta_c)|\le s_K(c)(\widehat q_{1-\alpha}+\eta)/\sqrt n\}\).

definitions.name: set-valued frontier inversion
definitions.construction: For each \(k\in\mathbb R\), retain every preference whose divergence band contains \(k\), namely \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_n(k)\), and take the union \(\widehat{\mathcal V}_n(k)\) of its welfare intervals; no derivative, branch choice, or local inverse enters the algorithm.

definitions.name: quadratic regret multiplier process
definitions.construction: Take the optimizer coordinates of \(G_n^*\), evaluate \(Q_n^*(c)=\tfrac12G^*_{n,\theta}(c)^\top\widehat H_c^{\mathrm{tot}}G^*_{n,\theta}(c)\), and use a shared conditional quantile of any prespecified continuous supremum functional of \(Q_n^*\).

statements.justification: The finite-action softmax derivatives expose both the envelope and polynomial entropy constants, while the one-dimensional optimizer path turns them into a quantitative conditional multiplier bound.
statements.gap: BelloniChernozhukovChetverikovWei2018 assumes a suitable estimated-score approximation and entropy bound; it does not derive this bound for fold-specific influences composed with a same-sample implicit softmax optimizer path.
statements.consumer: The open replacement question can focus on the shrinking empirical radius, after which a conditional maximal inequality yields multiplier replacement without treating overlapping training complements as independent.

statements.statement: For \(u\in\{0,1,2\}\), establish foldwise conditional nuisance bounds \(\max_{1\le\ell\le L}\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}\|E_P[\partial_\theta^u\{\widehat v_\theta^{(-\ell)}(O)-v_\theta(O)\}\mid\text{training complement}]\|\le C_{\mathrm{sm}}r_{m,n}r_{e,n}\) and \(\max_{1\le\ell\le L}\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}\|\partial_\theta^u\{\widehat v_\theta^{(-\ell)}-v_\theta\}\|_{P,2}\le C_{\mathrm{sm}}(r_{m,n}+r_{e,n})\). Prove \(\upsilon_n=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\) from uniform foldwise laws and localization, and derive the quantitative replacement template \(\delta_n\le C_{\mathrm{sm}}\{r_{m,n}+r_{e,n}+r_{m,n}r_{e,n}+\upsilon_n\}+o_{\mathbb P}(1)\). It follows that \(\delta_n=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\), equivalently \(\sup_{c\in\mathcal C}n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\|\widetilde\Psi_i(c)-\{\Psi_c(O_i)-\overline\Psi_n(c)\}\|^2=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\), for the fold-specific learned influences evaluated along the same-sample path \(\widehat\theta_c\). Together with the softmax-path entropy lemma, this must yield \(E_\xi[\sup_{c\in\mathcal C}\|n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\xi_i[\widetilde\Psi_i(c)-\{\Psi_c(O_i)-\overline\Psi_n(c)\}]\|\mid O_1,\ldots,O_n]=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\) despite overlapping training complements.
statements.justification: The product bound records orthogonal conditional bias, the sum bound records shrinking \(L^2(P)\) diameter, and the explicit path plug-in term isolates what same-sample optimization adds beyond pointwise DML.
statements.gap: BelloniChernozhukovChetverikovWei2018 assumes verifiable uniform score approximation conditions; it does not prove the empirical replacement radius for overlapping fold-specific nuisances composed with the same-sample softmax argmax path.
statements.consumer: The conditional multiplier theorem and every simultaneous post-selection frontier statement use this replacement bound.

statements.statement: For every \(c\in\mathcal C\), the first-order condition gives \(a_c=cg_c\), and hence \(\psi^W_c-c\psi^K_c=\phi^W_c-c\phi^K_c\) almost surely.
statements.justification: The identity separates oracle-path uncertainty from implemented-rule evaluation and is a sharp implementation check.
statements.gap: FangRidderXie2026 Theorem 5 derives fixed-\(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}\) efficient doubly robust optimizer inference but does not state this joint welfare--divergence cancellation along a penalty path.
statements.consumer: Software can test the identity at every plotted preference before trusting covariance or regret calculations.

statements.statement: Uniformly over \(c\in\mathcal C\), \(\sup_{c\in\mathcal C}\|\sqrt n\{\widehat\tau(c)-\tau(c)\}-n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n(\psi^\theta_c(O_i),\psi^W_c(O_i),\psi^K_c(O_i))\|=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\). Jointly, the two implemented-rule evaluation errors satisfy \(\sup_{c\in\mathcal C}|\sqrt n\{\widehat W(\widehat\theta_c)-W(\widehat\theta_c)\}-n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi^W_c(O_i)|=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\) and the analogous statement with \(K\) and \(\phi^K_c\). Therefore the full stack converges in \(C(\mathcal C)^{d+4}\) to \(G\) with kernel \(\Gamma\), and at every finite deterministic collection of penalty coordinates the optimizer coordinates jointly attain the semiparametric covariance bound generated by \(\psi_c^\theta\). On the common regular finite-action benchmark-centered softmax submodel, set FangRidderXie2026's optimization penalty to \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c\), so its reported preference is \(c_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}\). This is the uniform-in-penalty extension of the fixed-penalty efficient influence bound in its Theorem 1 and the efficient doubly robust optimizer limit in its Theorem 5.
statements.justification: On the common softmax submodel, a decision maker sees and selects from the whole preference curve; the contribution is the joint uniform process under explicitly maintained path-uniform interiority, three-derivative smoothness, and curvature, built on quantitative foldwise same-sample-path replacement.
statements.gap: FangRidderXie2026 Theorem 1 gives the efficient influence function and bound, while Theorem 5 gives the efficient doubly robust optimizer and its limit at fixed optimization penalty \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}>0\). Restricting its admissible-rule framework to \(\{\pi_\theta:\theta\in\Theta\}\) and mapping \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c\), equivalently \(c_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}\), the gap is a joint uniform oracle-and-implemented frontier process under separately stated stronger path-uniform regularity; generic indexed Z-estimation supplies tools but not this verified composition.
statements.consumer: The commitment-savings frontier in FangRidderXie2026 can be reported on the common regular softmax submodel with correlated uncertainty for every displayed preference rather than unrelated pointwise standard errors.

statements.statement: The replacement result gives \(\upsilon_n=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\), and therefore \(\sup_{c\in\mathcal C}\|\widehat H_c-H_c\|_{\mathrm{op}}=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\). Hence \(P(\mathcal E_n)\to1\) under \(\inf_{c\in\mathcal C}\lambda_{\min}(H_c)\ge h\). On \(\mathcal E_n\), \(\lambda_{\min}(\widehat H_c)\ge h/2\) for every \(c\), so \(\widehat H_c^{\mathrm{tot}}=\widehat H_c\) and \((\widehat H_c^{\mathrm{tot}})^{-1}=\widehat H_c^{-1}\) uniformly over \(\mathcal C\). Thus the measurable ridge fallback makes every finite-sample plug-in influence, covariance, and multiplier object total without changing any limiting law.
statements.justification: A declared totalization convention is necessary because a finite-sample empirical Hessian can be singular even when the population path is uniformly curved.
statements.gap: FangRidderXie2026 states fixed-penalty asymptotics and does not need a pathwise totalization convention for the proposed shared-multiplier implementation.
statements.consumer: Every reported covariance, multiplier draw, and regret draw remains mathematically defined on every sample, while the maintained curvature shows that the fallback is asymptotically inactive.

statements.statement: Construct \(\widetilde\Psi_i\), \(\widehat\Gamma\), and \(G_n^*\) with the common total ridge convention \((\widehat H_c^{\mathrm{tot}})^{-1}\). Under the explicit uniform estimated-influence replacement condition \(\delta_n=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\), the covariance estimator is uniformly consistent, \(\sup_{c,t\in\mathcal C}\|\widehat\Gamma(c,t)-\Gamma(c,t)\|\to_{\mathbb P}0\), and the conditional law of the stacked shared-multiplier process \(G_n^*\) given \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) converges in probability in bounded-Lipschitz distance on \(C(\mathcal C)^{d+4}\) to the law of \(G\). The event \(\mathcal E_n\) has probability tending to one and, on that event, the total ridge convention equals ordinary Hessian inversion simultaneously for every \(c\in\mathcal C\).
statements.justification: One shared multiplier path preserves covariance across preferences and all stacked coordinates, while the product-bias, sum-radius, path plug-in, and softmax-entropy bounds make the fold-specific plug-in step auditable.
statements.gap: BelloniChernozhukovChetverikovWei2018 validates estimated-score multipliers generically; the new theorem verifies its replacement and tightness requirements for the anchor's cross-fitted implicit optimizer path.
statements.consumer: An applied researcher can compute one critical value without re-solving the policy optimization inside each bootstrap draw.

statements.statement: For the fixed slack \(\eta>0\), \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}P\{(c,W(\theta_c),K(\theta_c))\in\widehat{\mathcal T}_n\text{ for every }c\in\mathcal C\}\ge1-\alpha\). Consequently, for every measurable selected preference \(\widehat c\in\mathcal C\), \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}P\{(\widehat c,W(\theta_{\widehat c}),K(\theta_{\widehat c}))\in\widehat{\mathcal T}_n\}\ge1-\alpha\).
statements.justification: The simultaneous event protects arbitrary data-dependent choice from the plotted curve without asserting conditional coverage after selection.
statements.gap: PolicyLearningWithConfidence2026 gives a general reporting-guarantee selection rule; this result instead covers the entire structural welfare--KL menu and every measurable selector from it.
statements.consumer: A planner may inspect all commitment-savings tradeoffs and choose a preference afterward while retaining the advertised unconditional coverage.

statements.statement: As a direct application corollary of RenTelschowSchwartzman2024 to the simultaneous tube event, for every \(k\in\mathbb R\) at once, \(\mathcal C(k)\subseteq\widehat{\mathcal C}_n(k)\) and \(\{W(\theta_c):c\in\mathcal C(k)\}\subseteq\widehat{\mathcal V}_n(k)\). The inclusions require neither injectivity nor a nonzero derivative of the displayed path.
statements.justification: This direct inverse-set application is a reporting corollary: retaining all compatible preferences avoids an artificial branch choice when the estimated curve is locally flat or numerically folds.
statements.gap: RenTelschowSchwartzman2024 already proves the eventwise inverse-set logic; this statement merely instantiates that result for the bivariate causal frontier and is not part of the novelty kernel.
statements.consumer: A planner specifying an acceptable KL departure obtains every preference and welfare value compatible with that target.

statements.statement: Benchmark normalization gives \(\pi_0(a\mid X)=b_a(X)\) almost surely for every \(a\in\mathcal A\) and makes \(K(\theta)\ge0\) for every \(\theta\in\Theta\). The regular optimizer path is continuously differentiable and satisfies \(H_c\theta_c'=-g_c\), \(\frac{d}{dc}K(\theta_c)=-g_c^\top H_c^{-1}g_c\le0\), and \(\frac{d}{dc}W(\theta_c)=c\frac{d}{dc}K(\theta_c)\). Under feature identification, either \(\theta_c=0\) for every \(c\in\mathcal C\) and the frontier is constant, or \(K(\theta_c)\) is strictly decreasing on \(\mathcal C\); thus a nonconstant maintained frontier has no self-intersection.
statements.justification: This result prevents the proposal from manufacturing singular geometry that its own assumptions rule out.
statements.gap: FangRidderXie2026 notes that restricted classes need not map preference one-to-one into divergence, but does not state this derivative characterization for the identifiable regular softmax path.
statements.consumer: The result tells applied users when ordinary monotone interpolation is safe and when the constant-path set-valued report is necessary.

statements.statement: The entire penalized-regret path has the uniform second-order reduction \(\sup_{c\in\mathcal C}|nR_n(c)-\tfrac12\{n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\psi^\theta_c(O_i)\}^\top H_c\{n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\psi^\theta_c(O_i)\}|=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\), so \(nR_n\Rightarrow Q\) in \(C(\mathcal C)\). Conditionally on the data, the totalized process \(Q_n^*\Rightarrow Q\), and conditional quantiles of continuous supremum functionals of \(Q_n^*\), enlarged by the fixed slack \(\eta\), yield simultaneous upper bands for \(R_n(c)\) that remain valid at \(\widehat c\). On the common regular finite-action benchmark-centered softmax submodel, set FangRidderXie2026's optimization penalty to \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c\), so its reported preference is \(c_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}\). This process is the uniform-in-penalty extension of its Theorem 2 fixed-penalty quadratic-regret law and its Theorem 5 efficient doubly robust quadratic-regret limit.
statements.justification: Under the note's explicitly stronger path-uniform smoothness and curvature conditions, the same first-order policy noise determines second-order loss across preferences, so separate fixed-positive-penalty regret approximations cannot support curve selection.
statements.gap: FangRidderXie2026 Theorem 2 gives the quadratic-regret law at one fixed optimization penalty \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}>0\), and Theorem 5 gives the efficient doubly robust optimizer and quadratic-regret limit. On the common finite-action benchmark-centered softmax subclass, with \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c\) and \(c_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}\), this theorem extends those fixed-penalty conclusions uniformly over the direct penalty path and adds conditionally valid shared-multiplier calibration; ChenFang2019 explains why a naive standard bootstrap is not enough.
statements.consumer: A planner choosing a displayed commitment-savings tradeoff receives a simultaneous upper bound on the statistical penalized-welfare loss of the fitted rule.

statements.statement: Non-novel sanity reduction: for every deterministic \(c\in\mathcal C\), evaluation of the uniform limits at \(c\) gives \(\sqrt n(\widehat\theta_c-\theta_c)\Rightarrow G_\theta(c)\) and \(nR_n(c)\Rightarrow\tfrac12G_\theta(c)^\top H_cG_\theta(c)\). Restrict FangRidderXie2026's admissible-rule framework to \(\{\pi_\theta:\theta\in\Theta\}\), set its optimization penalty to \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c\), and hence report \(c_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}\). The optimizer conclusion reduces to its Theorem 5 and the quadratic-regret conclusion reduces to its Theorems 2 and 5.
statements.justification: This is only a non-novel sanity reduction for auditing signs, Hessian normalization, and regret scaling against the published fixed-preference result.
statements.gap: No independent gap is claimed: the statement is the deterministic-penalty specialization to FangRidderXie2026 Theorems 2 and 5 on the common regular softmax submodel under \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c\) and \(c_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}\).
statements.consumer: Readers can audit signs, Hessian normalization, and regret scaling against the published theorem before using the new simultaneous procedure.

sampling_model.design: Independent and identically distributed observational or fixed-randomization sampling from \(P\); the known benchmark \(b_a\) is conceptually distinct from the observational propensity \(e_a\).
sampling_model.treatment: A fixed finite action set \(\mathcal A=\{0,\ldots,J-1\}\) under consistency, conditional exchangeability, and uniform overlap.
sampling_model.overlap: \(e_a(X)\ge\epsilon\) and \(b_a(X)\ge\epsilon_b\) almost surely for every action, with \(\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}b_a(X)=1\) almost surely.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: A fixed number of balanced folds; outcome and propensity learners are trained outside each evaluation fold, attain \(L^2(P_X)\) rates \(r_{m,n}\) and \(r_{e,n}\), and satisfy \(\sqrt n r_{m,n}r_{e,n}\to0\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: FangRidderXie2026 Theorem 1 derives the efficient influence function and bound, and Theorem 5 gives the efficient doubly robust optimizer at fixed optimization penalty \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}>0\); the common submodel sets \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c\), hence \(c_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}\), and restricts rules to \(\{\pi_\theta:\theta\in\Theta\}\).

FangRidderXie2026 Theorem 2 gives the fixed-penalty Hessian Gaussian quadratic-regret law, and Theorem 5 gives the efficient doubly robust optimizer and quadratic-regret limit; the common submodel sets \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c\), hence \(c_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}\), and restricts rules to \(\{\pi_\theta:\theta\in\Theta\}\).
Orthogonal function-valued Z-estimators admit uniform Bahadur representations and simultaneous estimated-score multiplier confidence bands under high-level approximation and entropy conditions.
Neyman orthogonality and cross-fitting deliver root-\(n\) inference for regular low-dimensional targets under nuisance product-rate conditions.
Gaussian and multiplier couplings approximate suprema of empirical processes under complexity and moment bounds.
A nonzero second derivative under first-order degeneracy yields a second-order limit and generally invalidates the standard bootstrap.
Directional differentiability permits uniform inference for statistics of optimized value functions when the marginal-optimization map is not Hadamard differentiable.
Confidence-penalized policy choice yields a simultaneous reporting guarantee and a regret bound over a policy set.
Inverting simultaneous confidence intervals gives simultaneous inner and outer coverage of inverse sets across all levels.
A smooth embedded one-dimensional curve in Euclidean space admits a simultaneous sausage-shaped confidence region.

tldr: On the common regular finite-action benchmark-centered softmax submodel of FangRidderXie2026, this proposal's direct KL penalty coordinate \(c\) maps to their optimization penalty \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c\), while their reported normalized preference is \(c_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}\). The field-level contribution is a quantitative empirical replacement template separating nuisance-product bias, nuisance-sum \(L^2(P)\) error, and same-sample path plug-in error; a checkable envelope and softmax-path entropy condition; the resulting joint uniform optimizer--welfare--divergence influence process and stacked shared-multiplier law; a simultaneous tube valid after any measurable penalty choice; and uniform Hessian-quadratic regret calibration. A measurable ridge fallback makes every finite-sample estimated influence, covariance, and multiplier object total and is uniformly inactive with probability tending to one. Path-uniform interiority, three-derivative smoothness, and curvature are stronger conditions maintained by this note, not conditions attributed to the fixed-penalty comparator. Benchmark weights form a positive probability kernel, so \(K\) is KL divergence and \(\pi_0=b\). Inverse-set reporting is a direct application corollary of RenTelschowSchwartzman2024, and the deterministic-penalty result is only a non-novel sanity reduction to FangRidderXie2026 Theorems 2 and 5.

project_justification.gap: FangRidderXie2026 Theorem 1 gives the efficient influence function and bound, Theorem 2 gives the fixed-penalty quadratic-regret law, Theorem 4 treats estimated-propensity IPW, and Theorem 5 gives the efficient doubly robust optimizer and quadratic-regret limit, all at fixed optimization penalty \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}>0\). With \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c\), hence \(c_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}\), and with its admissible rules restricted to the common finite-action benchmark-centered softmax subclass \(\{\pi_\theta:\theta\in\Theta\}\), it does not supply joint inference over the direct penalty path \(c\in\mathcal C\). Generic orthogonal-band theory assumes rather than verifies the uniform estimated-influence replacement needed for fold-specific learned influences evaluated along the same-sample implicit optimizer path.
project_justification.niche: The missing object on this common softmax submodel is a checkable path-entropy and replacement argument leading to one stacked shared-multiplier law that respects covariance across preferences, separates oracle-frontier uncertainty from fitted-rule evaluation, and protects selection from the displayed curve.
project_justification.fill: The project states the stronger path-uniform interiority, three-derivative smoothness, and curvature conditions explicitly; derives their finite-action softmax sufficient-condition routes; proves product-bias, sum-radius, path plug-in, envelope, and entropy bounds for the empirical replacement condition; uses a measurable ridge fallback that equals ordinary Hessian inversion uniformly with probability tending to one; obtains the joint uniform influence and shared-multiplier laws; forms a conservative simultaneous tube; and calibrates uniform second-order regret. The inverse correspondence is obtained afterward by direct application of RenTelschowSchwartzman2024.

related_work: FangRidderXie2026 supplies the admissible-rule framework and three-arm commitment-savings frontier. Its Theorem 1 gives the efficient influence function and bound, Theorem 2 the fixed-penalty quadratic-regret law, Theorem 4 the estimated-propensity IPW result, and Theorem 5 the efficient doubly robust optimizer and quadratic-regret limit. The common model here restricts that framework to its regular finite-action benchmark-centered softmax subclass \(\{\pi_\theta:\theta\in\Theta\}\): this proposal's direct penalty coordinate maps as \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c\), and the comparator's reported preference is \(c_{\mathrm{FRX}}=\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}=c/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}\). The new claim is uniformity over this direct penalty path, not a broader treatment class or a superset of their admissible rules. Their fixed-penalty interiority, two-derivative smoothness, and pointwise Hessian condition do not establish this note's uniform interiority, uniform three-derivative condition, or uniform curvature floor; those stronger hypotheses are explicitly introduced here, with compact-path and bounded-softmax sufficient-condition arguments. BelloniChernozhukovChetverikovWei2018 supplies the generic uniform Bahadur and estimated-score multiplier architecture; the present result is informed by that theorem and contributes explicit nuisance-product conditional-bias, nuisance-sum \(L^2(P)\)-radius, path plug-in, envelope, and softmax-path entropy bounds for fold-specific estimated influences along an implicit same-sample optimizer path. A single measurable ridge convention totalizes the estimated influence, covariance, shared-multiplier, and quadratic-regret objects and is shown to equal ordinary inversion uniformly on an event whose probability tends to one. ChernozhukovEtAl2018DML supplies orthogonality, foldwise conditioning, and nuisance product-rate logic for regular causal targets. ChernozhukovChetverikovKato2016 supplies Gaussian and multiplier coupling after deterministic entropy control. ChenFang2019 supplies the second-order delta method and the warning that standard bootstraps fail under first-order degeneracy; the proposed quadratic multiplier process is informed by that result. FirpoGalvaoParker2023 studies uniform inference after marginal optimization in nonregular value-function problems, whereas the explicitly maintained uniqueness and path-uniform curvature make the present implicit optimizer regular. PolicyLearningWithConfidence2026 already establishes a broad reporting-guarantee principle for selected policies, so this proposal claims only the KL-frontier-specific joint process and eventwise measurable-selection consequence. RenTelschowSchwartzman2024 supplies the inverse-set theorem, of which the frontier inversion is a direct application corollary; YamazoeNaito2024 supplies a geometric curve-region comparison. Neither inversion nor the deterministic-penalty reduction is part of the novelty kernel.
technical_internal_limitation: The central unresolved proof obligation is to derive \(\delta_n\le C_{\mathrm{sm}}\{r_{m,n}+r_{e,n}+r_{m,n}r_{e,n}+\upsilon_n\}+o_{\mathbb P}(1)\) and \(\upsilon_n=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\) for the fold-specific estimated influence stack evaluated along \(\widehat\theta_c\). The checkable envelope and softmax-path entropy lemma makes this shrinking radius sufficient for conditional multiplier replacement; it must not treat overlapping training complements as independent. The maintained path-uniform interiority, three-derivative smoothness, and curvature are stronger than the comparator's fixed-penalty regularity and remain explicit conditions. The measurable ridge fallback is a finite-sample totalization, not an assumption that empirical Hessians are invertible; its asymptotic irrelevance requires the stated uniform Hessian-consistency lemma and the good event \(\mathcal E_n\). The fixed positive direct-penalty interval excludes vanishing penalties, weak overlap, growing parameter dimension, adaptive sampling, and nonunique optimizers. The tube covers the oracle frontier and, when separately stacked, implemented-rule evaluation; these influences must not be interchanged. The quadratic claim concerns penalized regret, not unpenalized welfare loss.
honest_scope: The open content is the quantitative uniform empirical replacement bound for fold-specific estimated influences evaluated along the same-sample optimizer path, with nuisance-product bias, nuisance-sum \(L^2(P)\) error, and the explicitly defined path plug-in radius kept separate. The envelope and softmax-path entropy lemma makes that condition sufficient for the stacked shared-multiplier approximation. The implicit-function expansion and uniform quadratic mapping then deliver the joint frontier law, simultaneous post-selection tube, and uniform regret calibration under the note's explicitly stronger path-uniform interiority, three-derivative smoothness, and curvature conditions. A measurable ridge convention makes every plug-in object total, while uniform Hessian consistency and \(P(\mathcal E_n)\to1\) make it equal ordinary inversion simultaneously over the path asymptotically. RenTelschowSchwartzman2024 directly supplies the inverse-set corollary, while deterministic evaluation at one direct penalty is only a non-novel sanity reduction to FangRidderXie2026 Theorems 2 and 5 after setting \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c\), hence \(c_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}\), and restricting its admissible rules to \(\{\pi_\theta:\theta\in\Theta\}\). Genuine tangencies or self-intersections do not occur on a nonconstant frontier under the maintained identified softmax geometry. No broader treatment class, result for \(c\to0\), or Banach-space efficiency optimality for tube width is asserted.

seed_details.title: Uniform orthogonal limit theory for the optimizer and welfare--divergence path
seed_details.anchor_receipt: The anchor was read at Sections 1--4 and 7--8 and at Theorems 1, 2, 4, and 5 and their proofs. Theorem 1 gives the efficient influence function and bound, Theorem 2 the fixed-penalty quadratic-regret law, Theorem 4 estimated-propensity IPW, and Theorem 5 the efficient doubly robust optimizer and quadratic-regret limit. Its optimization coefficient is \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}\), while its reported preference is \(c_{\mathrm{FRX}}=\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}\); it plots rather than jointly infers this path.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The fixed-preference proof first changes where pointwise cross-fitted remainder control must become uniform after the estimated foldwise influence map is composed with the same-sample optimizer path.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for benchmark-centered softmax multiplier bootstraps, causal welfare--divergence confidence tubes, and cross-fitted optimizer-path processes found generic indexed orthogonal bands but no theorem for this stacked composition.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from BelloniChernozhukovChetverikovWei2018 because their uniform Bahadur and estimated-score multiplier theorems already cover function-valued orthogonal targets.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their generic theorem supplies the last approximation layer, but the random fold-specific class evaluated at an implicit same-sample argmax is not one of their verified applications; the publishable delta is a complete verification plus the optimizer, welfare, divergence, and implemented-value stack for the anchor's policy model.

seed_details.title: A conditionally calibrated quadratic-regret process over all positive penalty coordinates
seed_details.anchor_receipt: Theorem 2 and its proof were read. The proof is a fixed-\(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}\) second-order Taylor expansion, while Theorem 5 inserts the efficient doubly robust optimizer and quadratic-regret limit. The reported comparator index is \(c_{\mathrm{FRX}}=\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}\). No pathwise regret process or simultaneous critical value is supplied.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step is a uniform second-order expansion with one optimizer Gaussian process and one Hessian path, followed by a quadratic plug-in multiplier law rather than a naive recentered bootstrap.
seed_details.destination_search: The destination search paired uniform policy regret with second-order bootstrap inference. ChenFang2019 gives the general degeneracy warning and correction principle, but no indexed causal-policy quadratic process was found.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from FangRidderXie2026 pointwise regret plus the continuous mapping theorem.
seed_details.rebuttal: Uniform Taylor control and the quadratic map are routine only after the hard estimated-influence path bootstrap has been proved; as a standalone result this is too incremental, so it is retained only as a second theorem coupled to the uniform frontier process.

seed_details.title: Local-to-zero preference phase diagram between regular softmax and hard treatment choice
seed_details.anchor_receipt: The Introduction, Section 3, Section 5, and Conclusion were read. The paper explicitly separates fixed positive penalties from the nonregular zero-penalty boundary; uniform Hessian inversion is the first regular proof step that fails as the coefficient vanishes.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Replace uniform curvature by a local eigenvalue sequence and derive the normalization at which softmax smoothing bias, optimizer noise, and hard-policy nonregularity balance.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing vanishing KL temperature with treatment-rule asymptotics found Hirano--Porter's hard-rule endpoint and Crippa's smoothing-dependent threshold-policy regret, but no semiparametric transition for benchmark-centered assignment.
seed_details.red_team: A routine smoothing-parameter exercise combining the positive-penalty anchor with Crippa2025.
seed_details.rebuttal: The destination requires a new local experiment and a regime-dependent inverse-Hessian limit, not a substitution into either endpoint theorem; feasibility is nevertheless too uncertain for the first version.

seed_details.title: Semiparametric efficiency for the full preference-indexed frontier
seed_details.anchor_receipt: Section 3 and Theorems 1 and 5 were read. Theorem 1 derives the efficient influence function and bound, and Theorem 5 supplies the efficient doubly robust optimizer at each fixed \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}\); the paper does not formulate an efficiency ordering for confidence tubes or the full path as a Banach-valued parameter.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step is to define regularity and convolution bounds for the path in a function space rather than at finitely many deterministic coordinates.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for semiparametric efficiency bounds for policy-frontier confidence tubes found pointwise efficiency and generic functional inference, but no useful pathwise Loewner-minimal kernel or optimal-width theorem.
seed_details.red_team: Pointwise efficiency at every preference automatically gives efficiency of the path.
seed_details.rebuttal: That implication does not by itself order nonlinear tube widths, while a Banach-space convolution theorem may be formal rather than decision-relevant; the seed is dropped until an optimal confidence-loss criterion is identified.

seed_details.title: Matched minimax rates for the frontier under deteriorating overlap
seed_details.anchor_receipt: Assumption 2 and the efficiency calculations were read. The anchor requires support and integrability at a fixed preference and does not study a sequence of observational propensities approaching zero.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step is the influence-envelope bound: inverse propensities now grow with a primitive overlap exponent, changing both upper rates and least-favorable perturbations.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for weak-overlap minimax policy-frontier estimation found broad weak-overlap causal estimation but no matched rate for the KL optimizer and its bivariate frontier.
seed_details.red_team: This is generic weak-overlap theory with a softmax label.
seed_details.rebuttal: A genuinely new result would require a coupled lower bound for the optimizer and frontier geometry; the current substrate does not yet isolate that reduction, so the seed is dropped rather than padded.

seed_details.title: Choose a benchmark-proximity preference by a reporting-guarantee rule
seed_details.anchor_receipt: Section 2.2 and the Conclusion were read. The coefficient is a planner preference rather than a tuning parameter, and the paper reports its path without a data-driven selection rule.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step is to optimize a simultaneous lower confidence functional over the preference path and compare its welfare to an oracle preference subject to a divergence budget.
seed_details.destination_search: PolicyLearningWithConfidence2026 was opened through its current public manuscript. Its propositions already give reporting guarantees and regret bounds for confidence-penalized policy selection across a general policy set.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from PolicyLearningWithConfidence2026 by taking the policy set to be the softmax frontier.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds for the broad selection theorem; without a KL-specific sharper oracle relation, this seed is occupied and is dropped.

seed_details.title: Set-valued inversion of the welfare--divergence tube
seed_details.anchor_receipt: Section 2.2 was read. It warns that divergence in a restricted class need not be one-to-one in the preference. Direct differentiation in the maintained identifiable softmax model, however, gives a nonincreasing divergence path.
seed_details.proof_boundary: RenTelschowSchwartzman2024 already supplies the eventwise inversion theorem; the frontier construction is its direct bivariate application corollary and has no independent proof boundary.
seed_details.destination_search: RenTelschowSchwartzman2024 Theorem 1 was read and already turns simultaneous bands into simultaneous inner and outer inverse sets. YamazoeNaito2024 treats an embedded curve, not optimizer-generated values.
seed_details.red_team: Band inversion is an eventwise set inclusion, and the regular softmax path cannot genuinely self-intersect.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection defeats this as a standalone kernel. The construction remains only as a direct application corollary because it is useful at a constant path or under finite-sample near-tangency.

seed_details.title: Uniform frontier inference after adaptive experimental assignment
seed_details.anchor_receipt: The Introduction and related-literature discussion were read. They motivate adaptive experiments but expressly restrict the analysis to data from a fixed benchmark.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step replaces the i.i.d. empirical-process expansion by a uniform martingale-array expansion with predictable variance depending on both the preference and adaptive logging probabilities.
seed_details.destination_search: HadadEtAl2021 was opened and supplies variance-stabilized AIPW confidence intervals for fixed policy values under adaptive experiments; adaptive policy-learning papers supply regret but no joint optimizer-frontier tube.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate by applying HadadEtAl2021 pointwise over a compact one-dimensional index.
seed_details.rebuttal: Uniform predictable covariance, optimization, and estimated-path replacement are not pointwise consequences, but the change of sampling model is too large for this fixed-i.i.d. version.

seed_details.title: Finite-sample randomization inversion for a selected frontier point
seed_details.anchor_receipt: The fixed-benchmark experimental interpretation in Sections 1--2 was read. Its welfare target integrates heterogeneous potential outcomes under counterfactual rules rather than testing a sharp constant-effect null.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step would require a symmetry orbit that imputes the missing potential outcomes needed to recompute the learned frontier under assignment permutations.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing randomization or conformal inversion with learned welfare frontiers found symmetry methods for sharp counterfactual nulls, but no exact orbit for this composite heterogeneous-policy target.
seed_details.red_team: No exact finite-sample randomization distribution exists for the weak welfare null without additional effect restrictions.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds in the maintained model, so the required M17 lane has no credible survivor and is explicitly dropped.

literature_map.settled: FangRidderXie2026 Theorem 1 supplies the efficient influence function and bound, Theorem 2 the fixed-penalty quadratic-regret law, Theorem 4 estimated-propensity IPW, and Theorem 5 the efficient doubly robust optimizer and quadratic-regret limit at fixed \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}>0\). The corresponding common submodel sets \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c\), hence \(c_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}\), and uses \(\{\pi_\theta:\theta\in\Theta\}\).
literature_map.open_boundary: On that common finite-action softmax submodel, the paper's fixed-penalty interiority, two-derivative smoothness, and pointwise Hessian condition do not establish the stronger uniform interiority, uniform three-derivative condition, and uniform curvature floor maintained here; it also does not derive a joint optimizer--welfare--divergence process, a shared covariance kernel, or simultaneous post-selection coverage.

literature_map.settled: Uniform Bahadur representations and estimated-score multiplier bands are available for broad orthogonal Z-estimation problems, while cross-fitting controls learned nuisances for low-dimensional targets.
literature_map.open_boundary: The exact same-sample implicit optimizer path with overlapping fold-specific training complements and a stacked oracle-versus-implemented value process is not a verified application in these sources; the missing verification is organized into nuisance-product conditional-bias, nuisance-sum \(L^2(P)\)-radius, path plug-in, envelope, and entropy terms.

literature_map.settled: Coupling and multiplier approximations for suprema are available after a deterministic entropy envelope and suitable moments have been verified.
literature_map.open_boundary: The load-bearing work here is to replace the random estimated influence class by the true Lipschitz class uniformly in empirical \(L^2\), not to claim a new coupling theorem.

literature_map.settled: A second-order delta method yields quadratic limits, and a naive standard bootstrap is generally inconsistent when the first derivative vanishes but the second does not.
literature_map.open_boundary: The desired regret critical value is obtained from a shared Gaussian multiplier optimizer process and an estimated Hessian path, uniformly over preferences.

literature_map.settled: Simultaneous reporting guarantees can protect policies chosen after examining noisy estimates.
literature_map.open_boundary: The proposal does not claim the general selection principle; it supplies a model-specific joint tube whose event covers every measurable preference selected from the plotted KL frontier.

literature_map.settled: Inverting a simultaneous band yields simultaneous inverse-set coverage, and tubular regions exist for directly estimated embedded curves.
literature_map.open_boundary: Set-valued frontier inversion is a direct application corollary of RenTelschowSchwartzman2024 rather than part of the kernel; in the maintained regular softmax model, a geometry proposition rules out genuine self-intersections except for a constant path.

literature_map.settled: Directional-delta and resampling methods handle uniform statistics of value functions when marginal optimization is nonregular.
literature_map.open_boundary: Uniform uniqueness and curvature make the present optimizer path regular; the new burden is cross-fitted estimated-class replacement, not a new general derivative of the supremum map.
